The grimy window.
A grimy shirt.

more.def: Covered with dirt.
examples: His hands were grimy after fixing the bike.
The grimy window let in little light.
A grimy shirt lay on the floor.

easy.def: To smile very wide.
examples: He grinned at his dog.
She grins when she is happy.
We grinned at the funny joke.

more.def: To smile widely, showing your teeth, because you are happy or amused.
examples: Maya grinned from ear to ear when she saw her birthday cake.
The little boy grinned at the clown.
We all grinned when the puppy tripped over its own paws.

easy.def: A very wide smile.
examples: He had a big grin.
A grin spread on her face.
I saw a grin on my dad's face.

more.def: A wide smile that shows happiness or amusement.
examples: A huge grin spread across his face when he won the prize.
The cat in the story had a mysterious grin.
With a quick grin, she handed me the last cookie.

easy.def: To crush something into tiny bits.
examples: We grind wheat into flour.
Dad grinds coffee.
I ground the pepper.

more.def: To crush something into small bits or powder.
examples: The mill grinds wheat into flour.
Dad ground the pepper over my salad.
The machine grinds rocks into fine sand.

easy.def: To rub together with a rough sound.
examples: My teeth grind.
The gears grind.
The wheels ground on the road.

more.def: To rub or scrape together, making a rough sound.
examples: The gears ground against each other with a loud noise.
The truck's brakes ground to a stop.
He ground his heel into the dirt.

easy.def: A machine that crushes things into small bits.
examples: Dad used a coffee grinder.
The grinder is loud.
The grinder crushed the pepper.

more.def: A tool or machine that crushes or grinds things into small bits.
examples: Dad turned the pepper grinder over the salad.
A coffee grinder whirred in the morning.
The grinder in the shop was washed each evening.

easy.def: To hold something tightly.
examples: I grip the rope.
She gripped the railing.
The baby gripped my finger.

more.def: To hold something very tightly.
examples: I gripped the rope with both hands.
She gripped the railing on the icy stairs.
The tires grip the road.

easy.def: A tight hold.
examples: I have a good grip.
He lost his grip.
The grip on the bat is soft.

more.def: A firm, tight hold on something.
examples: He lost his grip on the slippery rope.
The bat has a rubber grip.
The baby had a strong grip on my finger.

easy.def: To complain about something.
examples: Do not gripe.
He griped about the rain.
She gripes a lot.

more.def: To complain in an annoyed way about something.
examples: Do not gripe about the weather; let's play inside.
He griped about the long line.
She griped that the soup was too cold.

easy.def: A complaint.
examples: I have a gripe.
What is your gripe?
A small gripe.

more.def: A complaint about something that annoys you.
examples: My biggest gripe is the long bus ride.
He had a gripe about the loud music.
What is your gripe about the new rule?

easy.def: Tiny bits of sand or stone.
examples: I got grit in my shoe.
There is grit on the floor.
The road has grit.

more.def: Tiny, hard bits of sand or stone, or the courage to keep trying.
examples: I felt grit between my teeth after the picnic on the beach.
She showed grit by finishing the race after she fell.
Workers spread grit on the icy road.

easy.def: A hot, soft food made from ground corn.
examples: I ate grits for breakfast.
The grits are creamy.
Grits and eggs.

more.def: A creamy hot cereal made from ground corn that is often eaten for breakfast in the southern United States.
examples: We ate grits and eggs for breakfast at the diner.
Grits are made from ground corn and cooked in water or milk.
She put butter and cheese in her bowl of grits.

easy.def: Full of tiny bits like sand.
examples: The sand is gritty.
The bread was gritty.
My shoe was gritty.

more.def: Containing small bits of sand or grit, or brave and determined.
examples: The sandwich was gritty from the beach.
The gritty floor needed sweeping.
She is a gritty player who never quits.

easy.def: A big brown bear.
examples: A grizzly caught a fish.
The grizzly is big.
We saw a grizzly.

more.def: A very large, strong brown bear with a hump on its back, found in North America.
examples: A grizzly waded into the river and caught a salmon.
The grizzly is a very large bear with a hump of muscle on its back.
Grizzlies sleep through the winter in dens.

easy.def: To make a long, low sound because you are unhappy.
examples: I groan when it is time for homework.
He groaned.
The class groaned.

more.def: To make a deep, low sound when you are in pain or do not like something.
examples: The class groaned when the teacher gave extra homework.
He groaned as he lifted the heavy box.
The old door groaned when I pushed it.

easy.def: A person who sells food in a store.
examples: The grocer sells fruit.
The grocer smiled.
Mom talked to the grocer.

more.def: A person who owns or works in a store that sells food.
examples: The grocer put our apples in a bag.
Mom asked the grocer for fresh bread.
The grocer set out boxes of oranges.

easy.def: Food and things bought at a store.
examples: We bought groceries.
The groceries are in the car.
Mom unpacked the groceries.

more.def: The food and household items that people buy at a grocery store.
examples: We bought groceries for the week.
Dad carried the groceries inside.
The groceries included milk and bread.

easy.def: A store that sells food.
examples: We went to the grocery.
The grocery sells milk.
Mom works at a grocery.

more.def: A store that sells food and everyday goods.
examples: We went to the grocery for milk.
The little grocery on the corner sells fresh fruit.
Mom works at the grocery store.

easy.def: To clean and brush an animal.
examples: I groom the horse.
She groomed the dog.
He grooms his hair.

more.def: To clean and brush an animal's coat, or to make yourself neat.
examples: I groomed the horse after our ride.
She groomed the dog's coat with a brush.
He groomed himself before the party.

easy.def: A man who is getting married.
examples: The groom wore a suit.
The bride and groom smiled.
The groom held her hand.

more.def: A man on his wedding day.
examples: The groom wore a gray suit.
The bride and groom cut the cake.
The groom smiled at his new wife.

easy.def: A long, narrow cut.
examples: The record has a groove.
A groove in the wood.
The wheel fits the groove.

more.def: A long, narrow channel or cut in a surface.
examples: The needle follows the groove on the record.
The wheel ran in a groove.
The wood had a deep groove.

easy.def: Very good or fun, in an old-fashioned way.
examples: That is a groovy hat.
A groovy song.
The party was groovy.

more.def: A slang word for something that is very good or stylish, used by people long ago.
examples: That is a groovy hat!
Grandpa played a groovy old song on his record player.
The party in the old movie was groovy.

easy.def: Very yucky.
examples: The smell is gross.
The old milk is gross.
That is gross!

more.def: Very unpleasant or disgusting.
examples: The rotten food was gross.
The smell from the trash was gross.
That is gross, so please wash your hands.

easy.def: A person in a bad mood.
examples: He is a grouch.
The grouch frowned.
Don't be a grouch.

more.def: A person who is often in a bad mood and complains.
examples: He was a grouch in the morning.
The old grouch frowned at the kids.
Nobody likes a grouch on a sunny day.

easy.def: In a bad mood.
examples: He is grouchy today.
The grouchy man frowned.
A grouchy cat.

more.def: Cranky and in a bad mood.
examples: He was grouchy because he was hungry.
The grouchy old man complained about the noise.
My little sister gets grouchy when she is tired.

easy.def: The earth that you walk on.
examples: The ground is wet.
Sit on the ground.
The apple fell to the ground.

more.def: The solid surface of the Earth that you stand and walk on.
examples: Snow covered the ground.
The ground shook when the truck passed.
She planted the seeds in the soft ground.

easy.def: A small animal that digs a burrow and sleeps all winter.
examples: A groundhog dug a hole.
Groundhog Day is in February.
The groundhog came out.

more.def: A small, furry animal that digs underground burrows and sleeps through the winter; it is also called a woodchuck.
examples: A groundhog dug a burrow under the garden fence.
On Groundhog Day, people watch to see if the groundhog sees its shadow.
The groundhog stuffed itself with clover before winter.

easy.def: Some people or things together.
examples: A group of kids played.
A group of ducks swam by.
We sat in a group.

more.def: A number of people, animals or things that are together.
examples: A group of students waited for the bus.
A group of whales swam past the boat.
Sort the shapes into three groups.

easy.def: To put things together in sets.
examples: Group the toys by color.
She grouped the cards.
We grouped the blocks.

more.def: To put people or things together into sets.
examples: Group the buttons by color.
The teacher grouped us in pairs.
She grouped the animals by where they live.

easy.def: A set of things put together.
examples: A grouping of trees.
The grouping is by color.
A grouping of desks.

more.def: A set of people or things put together as a group.
examples: A grouping of desks faced the board.
Put the animals in a grouping by size.

easy.def: A small group of trees.

The grove is shady.

more.def: A small group of trees growing close together.
examples: We picnicked in a grove of pine trees.
The orange grove smelled sweet.
A grove of oaks stood by the stream.

easy.def: To get bigger.
examples: Plants grow in the sun.
My baby brother grows fast.
The puppy grew bigger.

more.def: To become bigger or taller as time passes.
examples: Sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up.
The town grew as more families moved in.
My hair has grown a lot since last spring.

easy.def: To plant something and take care of it.
examples: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
Farmers grow corn.
She grew beans in a cup.

more.def: To plant seeds or young plants and take care of them until they are ready.
examples: Grandpa grows vegetables behind his house.
Farmers in this valley grow apples and pears.
We grew sunflowers for the school fair.

easy.def: To slowly become a certain way.
examples: It grows dark early in winter.
She grew tired of waiting.
He grew sleepy in the car.

more.def: To slowly change until something is a certain way.
examples: The sky grew dark as the storm came closer.
The puppy grew sleepy after its walk.
As the music grew louder, the crowd began to clap.

easy.def: A person who grows plants.
examples: The grower sells apples.
A grower plants seeds.
The grower is a farmer.

more.def: A person who grows plants or crops, especially to sell.
examples: The grower sold apples at the market.
A tomato grower planted rows of seedlings.
The grower picked the ripe peaches.

easy.def: To make a low, angry sound.
examples: The dog growled.
The bear growls.
The tiger growled.

more.def: To make a low, rough sound in the throat, as an angry animal does.
examples: The dog growled at the stranger.
A bear growled in the cave.
My stomach growled because I was hungry.

easy.def: A person who is not a child.
examples: Ask a grownup for help.
A grownup read us a story.
The grownups sat at the table.

more.def: A person who is fully grown, rather than a child.
examples: Please ask a grownup before you use the stove.

easy.def: Getting bigger.
examples: The plant's growth is fast.
The growth of the town.
Plants need sun for growth.

more.def: The process of getting bigger or developing.
examples: The plant's growth was fast in spring.
The growth of the town brought new schools.
Sunlight and water help plant growth.

examples: A bird pulled a fat grub from the soil.
A grub is a baby beetle that lives underground.

easy.def: Food.
examples: Time for grub!
We ate some grub.
The grub was good.

more.def: A slang word for food.
examples: It is time for grub!

The grub at the picnic was great.

easy.def: Dirty.
examples: His hands are grubby.

A grubby shirt.

more.def: Slightly dirty or messy.
examples: His hands were grubby after playing in the dirt.
The grubby puppy rolled in the mud.
She wore a grubby shirt.

easy.def: A bad feeling you keep about someone.
examples: He held a grudge.
Do not keep a grudge.
The grudge lasted.

more.def: A feeling of anger that you keep for a long time because of something that happened.
examples: He held a grudge against his brother.
It is best not to keep a grudge.

easy.def: Very hard and tiring.
examples: The hike was grueling.

more.def: Extremely tiring and demanding.
examples: The grueling climb took all day.

easy.def: Rough and grumpy in the voice.

more.def: Rough or harsh in the voice or manner.

easy.def: To complain in a low voice.
examples: Do not grumble.

more.def: To complain in a low, unhappy voice.
examples: The old farmer grumbled about the price of corn.

easy.def: A low complaint.
examples: I heard a grumble.
There was a grumble.

more.def: A low sound of complaint, or a low rumbling noise.
examples: I heard a grumble from the back of the room.
There was a grumble of thunder in the distance.

easy.def: A person who is often in a bad mood.
examples: He is a grump today.
Do not be a grump.
The grump frowned.

more.def: A person who is often cross and complains a lot.
examples: He was a grump before breakfast.
The old grump complained about the noise.

easy.def: In a bad mood.
examples: I am grumpy when I am tired.

more.def: Easily annoyed and in a bad mood.
examples: He is always grumpy before he has eaten breakfast.

examples: The pig grunts.

more.def: To make a short, rough sound like a pig, or when you work hard.
examples: The pig grunted at the fence.
